newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas futures end near session highs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas futures end near session highs.

text.p: NYMEX Hub natgas futures ended firmer Friday amid stronger cash, but traders' expectations for next week were mixed.
May settled 3.7 cents higher at $1.942 per mmBtu, just 0.3 cent shy of the session's high. June finished up 3.2 cents at $1.998, while other deferreds were one to three cents higher.

"I think we're still pretty bearish. The funds in the market Monday should put downward pressure on the market," one trader said, adding he expected spring-like weather to also pressure the market next week.
However, other traders viewed May's close near session highs as bullish.
"It finished up on the highs. It also shrugged off bearish AGAs earlier this week. Cash was also pretty stable even though it was for a weekend," one Houston-based trader said.
"There's not as much fund length in the market. It doesn't affect the market as much as it used to," he added.

Technically, support in May was still pegged at $1.85, $1.825, $1.78 and the contract low of $1.71, which have held for more than a week. Further support was at $1.65-1.70. Resistance was still seen at $1.95-1.97 and $2.04-2.05.
NYMEX said an estimated 6,379 Hub contracts traded. Open interest for April 3 jumped 2,816 to 168,741.

U.S. Gulf Coast cash prices were at a slight discount to futures as Henry Hub gas traded mostly at $1.88-1.92, up about three cents. Prices on the Midcontinent pipes also gained a couple of cents to the mid-$1.70s, with Chicago city-gate quoted at $1.90. In response to milder temperatures, New York city-gate prices fell another two to three cents to $2.08-2.16.

Temperatures in the East and upper Midwest are expected to remain normal to above normal through the weekend before turning cooler early next week. Weather in the southern plains, Texas and parts of the West are expected to be cooler-than-normal, which will likely limit air-conditioning demand.
No Permian or Alberta natgas futures traded.
On KCBT, May finished up two cents at $1.78, while deferreds were one to three cents higher. The East/West spread widened by 2.2 cents to 16.2 cents (NYMEX premium).

Physical prices in the Permian basin slipped two cents to the high-$1.60s to low-$1.70s as cooler weather moved into the region and Pacific Gas and Electric's 1,073 megawatt Diablo Canyon nuclear unit 2 was expected to return to the grid today.
